subject: Lumina Health — open-model fit & next steps (post-call recap)
summary: Post-call recap: Lumina Health currently uses OpenAI + Anthropic for chat and embeddings. Main pain points are PHI/BAA needs, latency at scale, and cost unpredictability. They are open to an on-prem/private option and need model compatibility (function-calling, streaming, embeddings). Shortlist: Llama 2 chat variants, Mistral Instruct, and Falcon-family inference candidates. Next steps: share benchmark corpus, schedule technical deep-dive, confirm security evidence and BAA timeline.
messages:
From: Alex Bennett <alex.bennett@luminahealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Sinha <priya@luminahealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Intro + quick context before today's call

Thanks Jasmine — quick context from our side before the call: we run two main LLM flows in production. 1) clinical summarization for clinician notes (OpenAI gpt-4.1 for chat + streaming) — about 18k tokens/day, spikes to ~9 concurrent sessions during peak; 2) patient triage embeddings/search (Anthropic for embeddings today) — ~25k embeddings/month.

Big constraints: PHI (HIPAA) so any move needs a BAA; latency target for clinician UX is ~<200ms tail for generation; cost has become unpredictable with burst usage and we'd like a 50%+ reduction target on per-token bill.

Happy to run numbers on our end during the call. See attached usage export for a high-level view.

— Alex
Director of Engineering, Lumina Health
attachments: lumina-prod-usage-agg-0626.csv (csv, 120KB)
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Bennett <alex.bennett@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Priya Sinha <priya@luminahealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T15:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + quick context before today's call — recap + proposed next steps

Thanks Alex — great conversation earlier. Quick recap from our side + agreed next steps so everyone has the same view.

What we heard (pain points):
- PHI / compliance: customer must have a BAA and evidence for SOC2/audit logs.
- Latency under load: current tail latency spikes causing clinician UX issues — target <200ms (you said median currently ~120–150ms, tails up to ~700ms during spikes).
- Cost predictability: large bursts drive up spend; looking for at least ~50% reduction in per-token costs or predictable committed capacity.
- Function-calling & streaming: critical for summarization pipeline (we need streaming + structured function outputs preserved).
- Embeddings compatibility: must preserve similarity scores and be able to re-run historical vectors with minimal drift.

Current stack we confirmed:
- Chat + generation: OpenAI (chat + function-calling)
- Embeddings: Anthropic/third-party embeddings provider
- Orchestration: internal microservices, Redis-based KV cache for conversation state, S3 for transcripts
- Traffic: steady daily baseline, bursts during clinic hours (peak concurrency ~9–12 sessions)

Preliminary model fit (shortlist to evaluate):
- Llama 2 chat (quantized variants) — for instruction/chat parity and embeddings parity via fine-tuning/adapter layers.
- Mistral Instruct / Mistral-chat family — competitive inference cost with strong instruction-following.
- Falcon-40B / Falcon-180B-instruct (quantized candidate) — good token throughput with proven instruction tuning.

Constraints to validate technically:
- Streaming + function-calling parity (we will run tests to validate structured responses and evented streaming).
- Embeddings stability (we will re-embed a sample set and compare recall/precision against current provider).
- Memory & KV cache compatibility (hot-prefix cache semantics — preservation of chat K/V).
- Cost: model quantization/packing and Redwood Optimize recommendations to hit cost target.

Action items we agreed on:
1) Lumina -> share a redacted sample prompt set + 100 anonymized transcripts for benchmarking (Alex) — due by 2026-07-23.
2) Redwood -> run an initial compatibility benchmark: streaming/function-calling, embeddings drift test, and latency p95/p99 on a 10-concurrent session simulated load (Rishi / Dev) — deliverables by 2026-07-30.
3) Security: Lumina to share completed security questionnaire (Priya) and we will surface SOC2 artifacts + BAA draft (Jasmine) — BAA draft by 2026-07-26.
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Lumina infra/security + Redwood infra (30–45m) — target week of 2026-07-27 (Dev to propose slots).

Attachments: I pulled the usage export you attached into the bench plan. We'll confirm what we need for the embeddings re-run.

If that captures it, I'll open a HubSpot deal record with the MAP and next-step tasks.

Thanks again — positive fit IMO; we'll validate on the technical pass.

— Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Sinha <priya@luminahealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Bennett <alex.bennett@luminahealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lumina Health — open-model fit & next steps (post-call recap)

Thanks Jasmine — quick clarification items from security:

On Fri, Jul 19, 2026 at 3:27 PM Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> - Security: Lumina to share completed security questionnaire (Priya) and we will surface SOC2 artifacts + BAA draft (Jasmine) — BAA draft by 2026-07-26.

We can share the completed questionnaire (attached). A couple follow-ups:
- Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in private deployments? We may need that for PHI encryption at rest.
- For the SOC2 artifacts, will we get an attestation or the full report under NDA?
- Data retention: we need options to set retention to 30/90/365 days for logs/transcripts; is that configurable per-namespace?

I'll attach our security questionnaire (redacted) — please confirm receipt.

— Priya
Head of Security Engineering, Lumina Health
attachments: lumina-security-questionnaire.pdf (pdf, 350KB)
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Bennett <alex.bennett@luminahealth.com>, Priya Sinha <priya@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lumina Health — open-model fit & next steps (post-call recap)

Priya / Alex — received the questionnaire, thanks. Short answers to your security follow-ups (we will include these in the BAA/MAP doc):

- Customer-managed keys: yes, supported for Redwood Private deployments (KMS integrations + HSM option for on-prem). We'll include the integration matrix in the security packet.
- SOC2 artifacts: we can provide the SOC2 Type II report under NDA and an attestation as part of the commercial/legal packet; our legal team will coordinate the limited-scope share.
- Data retention: retention windows are configurable per namespace at deployment time (30 / 90 / 365) and adjustable via the Console; we will propose defaults and an architecture note in the deep-dive.

Next actions on our calendar:
- Rishi + Dev will run the technical bench and share a short report (p95/p99 latency, streaming parity, embeddings drift) by 2026-07-30.
- I'll circulate a BAA draft and Redwood security packet by 2026-07-26.
- Dev to propose 2x 30–45m slots for infra deep-dive for the week of 2026-07-27.

If any of the timelines feel aggressive on your side, flag them and we'll adjust. Otherwise I'll open the HubSpot MAP and attach the two files you shared.

— Jasmine
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
